evidence: Atomic force microscopy is used to measure the grain-size (D) and arithmetic mean roughness (Ra) of PbS, PbI2, and MAPbI3, as detailed in Figure 1b. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the elemental presence of Pb, I, S, and N in each of the expected films: PbS, PbI2, and MAPbI3. Through a complementary X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, we further confirmed the material composition at each step and demonstrated that the conversion processes of PbS to PbI2, and PbI2 to MAPbI3, is complete. A 45° scanning electron microscope image shows the polycrystalline grains on the surface of the fabricated MAPbI3 films. The absorption coefficient, α(E), is shown in Figure 3b. The temperature-dependent PL is shown in Figure 3c. To elucidate gain dynamics, we studied the transient evolution of the film absorption using ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy.
